messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2 (11:45 UTC). Auto-page to oncall.

sanjay: I got the page, pulling metrics now. seeing p50 ~120ms, p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~4.8s for streaming tail. websocket stalls + reconnects spiking.

maya: customers reporting degraded chat sessions and slow tokenization. dashboard shows high request queuing on inference gateways in az-b and az-c.

chris: logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts from outbound NAT to 3rd-party DNS resolvers and also increase in TCP retransmits. packet loss counters up on cross-AZ paths.

sanjay: running quick checks. `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide` shows a few gateway pods migrating across nodes. `ss -s` shows surge in syn retries.

sanjay: running trace to one affected node: ```
traceroute -n 10.0.1.45
1 10.0.1.45 0.123 ms
2 10.1.254.1 2.345 ms
3 52.16.10.1 30.234 ms (cross-zone NAT)
``` suggests an egress hop with high latency.

elaine: our NAT pool in eu-west-2 appears to be at ~95% ephemeral port utilization per cloud-metrics. conntrack entries also near limit on the NAT instances.

opsbot: runbook hint: if ephemeral ports exhaustion -> add NAT gateways / increase ephemeral range / rotate source IPs.

chris: also seeing lots of DNS retries; resolvers in that region show increased response times. Could be NAT queuing causing packets to be dropped and TCP handshake slowdown.

sanjay: quick hypothesis: cross-AZ path through shared NAT/egress gateway is getting buffered/dropping -> TLS handshake spikes and streaming stalls due to backpressure on long-lived websockets.

maya: customer-impact snapshot: ~18% of active streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s in last 10m. Affected tenants: several Dedicated and Hosted customers pinned to eu-west-2.

sanjay: mitigation plan (short): 1) divert new traffic to eu-central1 via smart-routing for non-data-residency tenants, 2) scale up NAT instances in eu-west-2, 3) increase conntrack/ephemeral limits and rotate source IPs to relieve port exhaustion, 4) enable aggressive TCP retransmit tuning on gateways.

chris: I can flip smart-routing for non-EU-bound customers. prepping an allowlist to keep regulated tenants in-place.

elaine: scaling NAT autoscaling group now. increasing desired count +2. applying conntrack sysctl tweak on nodes: ```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288``` and increasing ephemeral port range: ```sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"10240 65535\"```.

sanjay: applying quick iptables conntrack cleanup on one NAT to test: `conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 480k, then `conntrack -F` (roll one instance) — doing canary restart.

opsbot: NOTE: canary NAT restart will drop existing ephemeral mappings, long-lived websockets may reconnect. choose low-risk AZ.

sanjay: doing canary in az-c. rolling restart initiated.

chris: smart-route cutover started for non-compliant tenants: `route-policy apply smart-route eu-west-2 -> eu-central-1 (non-resident)` — monitoring.

customer-ops: can you prep a short customer update? ops needs wording for affected Dedicated customers.

maya: draft msg: "We observed an egress network path degradation in eu-west-2 causing elevated latency and streaming reconnects. We are actively mitigating by scaling egress gateways and redirecting non-resident traffic. Investigating root cause; will update in 30m." comments?

customer-ops: looks good, add note about potential reconnects and suggestion to retry idempotently.

chris: after canary NAT restart, p99 dropped from ~4.8s to ~1.6s in that AZ. overall cluster p99 now ~2.2s. some improvement but still above SLO.

sanjay: continuing mitigations: increased NAT count +2 done, conntrack tuned cluster-wide, ephemeral range updated, smart-routing in progress. also setting temporary per-tenant routing to avoid cross-AZ hairpin for streaming (prefer same-AZ egress where possible).

elaine: cloud provider telemetry shows transient overload on the shared egress appliance in az-b (queue length high). we've submitted a support ticket (INC-88911) and requested priority handling.

opsbot: runbook step executed: adjusted SLO alerts to avoid noisy paging during mitigation window. manual paging still enabled for new customer-impact symptoms.

sanjay: p95 steady around 400-600ms now, p99 ~1.8s. streaming stalls reduced by ~70% since start. still monitoring for packet loss tail.

diana: I'm shadowing for handoff in 90m, will take over if still open. oncall notes: check cloud INC-88911 for provider updates, keep smart-routing toggles handy.

chris: provider responded: they saw internal NAT appliance queueing caused by bursty cross-zone egress; they've moved some capacity and we should see continued improvement over next 15-30m.

sanjay: marking timeline: root cause likely egress appliance queueing + conntrack/ephemeral port pressure amplified by cross-AZ hairpinning. mitigation: scale NAT, conntrack/ephemeral tuning, smart-route diversion, provider capacity adjustments.

maya: customer impact summary for postmortem: 12 enterprise customers impacted, peak affected sessions ~18% of active streaming sessions, no data loss, reconnects observed. Action items: 1) add additional regional NAT capacity, 2) auto-scale conntrack thresholds, 3) update smart-routing policy to avoid hairpin by default, 4) add synthetic streaming monitors across AZs.

customer-ops: sending updates to affected customers now. templated note prepared and will be posted in status page.

sanjay: closing page for now, continuing monitoring. handoff to diana at 90m or earlier if regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; service SLOs partially restored. Incident transitioning to investigation state. Reference: INC-88911."
